newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-SOUTH AMERICAN QUALIFIERS THROWN WIDE OPEN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SOUTH AMERICAN QUALIFIERS THROWN WIDE OPEN.

text.p: The South American World Cup qualifying competition was thrown wide open on Sunday when Peru and Bolivia both won to rekindle their hopes and old foes Uruguay and Argentina drew 0-0 in Montevideo.
Only two points now separate third-place Argentina from eighth-place Chile as the marathon competition, in which the nine teams play each other twice, nears the halfway mark.
The top four teams in the group qualify for the 1998 World Cup in France, with Brazil exempt from the qualifying tournament as holders.
In the old days, Uruguay and Argentina would have expected to meet little resistance from the other South American nations.
This time, however, they have found themselves slugging it out with teams such as Peru, Bolivia and Ecuador and playing second fiddle to group leaders Colombia and Paraguay.

The relatively poor campaigns of the two great rivals added extra spice to Sunday's meeting -- their first-ever in a World Cup qualifier -- but despite the tension there was no trouble and only three players were booked.
Uruguay had slightly the better of the game in which the performance of Ignacio Gonzalez hinted that Argentina may have finally ended their goalkeeping troubles.

The highlight of a solid display by Gonzalez, the fifth goalkeeper to be used by Argentine coach Daniel Passarella in the last year, was a spectacular seventh minute save from veteran Enzo Francescoli.
"We overcame a stiff test and kept third place in a very tough qualifying contest," said Passarella.
The result kept Argentina ahead of Uruguay on goal difference. Both have ten points.
Peru, Bolivia and Ecuador all have nine points after Peru beat Chile 2-1 in Lima and Bolivia beat Ecuador 2-0 in La Paz.
Peru overcame Chile with first half goals by Flavio Maestri and Roberto Palacios. Ivan Zamorano grabbed a consolation for Chile, who have eight points, two minutes from time.

Bolivia have failed to make the most of playing at 3,600 metres above sea level, drawing their last three home games, but wrapped up Sunday's game in the first 12 minutes with goals by Jaime Moreno and Marco Etcheverry.

The Bolivians won all their home games on their way to reaching the 1994 World Cup, with Brazil among their victims, and their failure to repeat the performance may seriously undermine their hopes of qualifying again.
Paraguay, who last reached the World Cup finals in 1986, moved four points ahead of Argentina with a 2-0 win away to lightweights Venezuela, who are propping up the table with a meagre one point.
Miguel Benitez and Julio Enciso scored in each half for Paraguay, who were missing their inspirational goalkeeper-cum-free kick specialist Jose Luis Chilavert through suspension.
Paraguay cut the gap between themselves and leaders Colombia, who did not play, to three points.
